title: Project 2: Persuasive or Deceptive Visualization?
description: This project explores the boundaries of ethical data visualization by creating two opposing charts based on the same dataset regarding the NYPD stop-and-frisk policy. We utilized various persuasive and deceptive design tactics to demonstrate how charts can manipulate interpretation either for or against a proposition. Ultimately, the project highlights the ethical responsibility of designers to present data without distortion.

title: Project 1: Food Processing Score
description: This visualization highlights the distribution of food processing scores (FPro) across Target, Walmart, and Whole Foods to reveal differences in inventory healthfulness. By combining violin plots with box plots and color-coded gradients, the design clearly contrasts the predictable, highly processed selections of Walmart and Target against Whole Foods' varied offerings. It provides an intuitive, macro-level view of product category differences among major retailers.

title: Predicting Google Play Store Rankings
description: This data science project examines the quantitative factors—such as total ratings, installs, and growth rates—that predict a mobile game's rank within genre-specific Top 100 charts on the Google Play Store. The team performed extensive data cleaning and utilized machine learning models like SVM and Random Forest regressors to identify ranking patterns. The analysis revealed that overall rank is most strongly associated with engagement volume metrics, providing valuable insights for game developers seeking to improve discoverability.

title: blueprint
description: blueprint is an interactive code editor extension that helps developers visualize and understand any codebase at multiple scales using expandable knowledge graphs. It uses AI compression models to trace dependencies, summarize features, and proactively identify vulnerabilities before changes are made. By making code relationships visually accessible, the tool brings trust and scale to modern AI-assisted vibe engineering.

title: CiteTrace
description: CiteTrace transforms large collections of research papers into interactive knowledge graphs, allowing users to intuitively visualize and interpret complex academic relationships. The platform features an end-to-end RAG pipeline and similarity-scoring models to help researchers dive deep into document connections and discover hidden themes. By making research landscapes navigable at a glance, it significantly streamlines the literature review process.

title: Bouncer
description: Bouncer is an AI-powered consumer risk assessment tool that provides business owners with intelligent access control using publicly available information. By integrating deep search APIs with Claude and Gemini models, the platform generates safe, thoroughly explained risk-level summaries while reducing bias. It demonstrates how public data can be ethically leveraged for social good through a visually pleasing and secure user management dashboard.

title: PillSnap
description: PillSnap is a mobile-friendly web application that allows users to snap a photo of any pill to accurately identify it and access up-to-date FDA drug information. Leveraging a fine-tuned Gemini API and live data scraping, the app provides critical warnings about potential drug and food interactions. It empowers patients—especially the elderly and disabled—to safely manage multiple medications and avoid dangerous misuse.

title: CARP (Catch, Analyze, Record, & Profit)
description: CARP is a comprehensive platform designed to optimize the fishing value chain using AI-powered insights, an interactive fish location map, and real-time market analysis. Leveraging a Gemini-powered chatbot, algorithmic fish ranking, and browser-use agents, the app helps fishers maximize profit by analyzing over 50,000 data points across 5,700 species. Additionally, the system includes a dual-purpose health tracker and brace to monitor carpal tunnel indicators, ensuring user well-being while fishing.

title: Efficient optimization of COHERENT detector design parameters with RESUM
description: This study introduces the Rare Event Surrogate Model (RESUM) to optimize shielding configurations for the COH-Ar-750 detector. By integrating a Conditional Neural Process with a Multi-Fidelity Gaussian Process, RESUM significantly reduces the need for computationally expensive Monte Carlo simulations when predicting neutron background rates. The surrogate model achieves high predictive accuracy while requiring over 70% less simulation data, offering an efficient tool for rare event search experiments.

title: Assistive Eyewear for Crosswalk Navigation
description: This project integrates the YOLOv4-tiny object detection model with a custom Raspberry Pi-powered eyewear apparatus to assist legally blind individuals with crosswalk navigation. By identifying crosswalk markers, traffic signals, and vehicles, the system provides real-time audio feedback to help users safely navigate intersections. Evaluated using the System Usability Scale, the affordable prototype demonstrates how lightweight deep learning models can be effectively deployed on edge devices to improve accessibility.

title: Fake News Identification via CNN-RNN
description: This study advances deep learning solutions for fake news detection by combining a CNN-RNN text classifier with a complementary URL feature classifier. The hybrid model was trained and evaluated on multiple datasets, achieving high accuracies across general and COVID-19 news categories. An interactive graphical user interface (GUI) was also developed using Python Dash to make these advanced fact-checking tools accessible to the general public.

title: Diagnosing Knee Injuries in MRI Scans
description: This research project investigates the use of convolutional neural networks to automate the diagnosis of knee injuries, such as ACL and meniscal tears, from MRI scans. Using TensorFlow and the RetinaNet object detection model, the system is trained on extensive MRI datasets to identify abnormalities and reduce human diagnostic errors. Ultimately, the automated approach aims to prioritize high-risk patients and provide a reliable, unbiased tool to assist radiologists in clinical decision-making.
